chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: How long Fambro's band lasted and Duke taking its men
summary: Jones was with Fambro's Ellington-oriented band about three years; Nat Jones and Sax Mallard drifted back from Ellington.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: In -- about Tony[Fambreau's]band, how long did it last? How many years did he have a band?
Let me see. Now, John Levy probably would know this, because John was playing bass with it. I guess I was with Tony[Fambreau's]band about three years or so, you know.
Was the band around quite a long time in Chicago?
Yeah, well there were some guys that preceeded me on piano, you know.
But it was Ellington orientated, you know.
You know, they had that -- because the best proof of it, Duke started taking Tony's sidemen.
And they didn't stay with Ellington's band, because -- there was one guy named Nat Jones who was a great clarinetist and a great alto player, another named
Sax Mallard who was great also. And had they stayed in Ellington's band with Johnny Hodges there, it would have been World War III.
But they all came -- they all drifted back home, you know.
